title: ReviewVerdict v2
description: Independent-review verdict. v2 adds the three fields a bounded review loop needs in order to stop for the right reason: `blocking` (separated from severity), `subject` (deliverable vs tooling vs the review's own scaffolding, per verification-principles V43), and `finding_kind` + `mechanism` (so recurrence is counted by mechanism rather than by tally, per V25/V30/V41). It also loosens v1's rule that an approval must carry zero findings: an approval may now carry non-blocking findings, which is the whole point of separating the two. A v1 document does not validate against this schema — `schema_version` is a const — and a loop registered at v2 must refuse a v1 submission rather than coercing it.

loop_id.description: Identifies the review loop this verdict belongs to. Required because a recurrence threshold cannot live in prose (V41): the ledger keys its persisted counts on this value, and a verdict that does not say which loop it belongs to cannot be matched against previous rounds.

round.description: 1-based round number within loop_id. The ledger, not the reviewer, is authoritative if these disagree.

agent.description: The reviewing agent. Must not be the agent that produced the work under review; the ledger enforces this, and the schema records it so the violation is auditable after the fact.

severity.description: How bad it is if it is real. Deliberately NOT the same axis as `blocking`: v1 conflated them, so a Critical-but-out-of-scope observation and a Medium-that-must-be-fixed-first were indistinguishable.

blocking.description: True = the verdict cannot be `approved` while this stands. A finding may be Critical and non-blocking (real, but out of this loop's scope) or Medium and blocking (small, but it defeats a control). Only blocking findings gate approval and only blocking findings count toward the mechanism-class stop.

subject.description: What the finding is about. `review-scaffolding` covers the review apparatus itself — the prompt wording, the ledger schema, receipt naming, the gate script's error strings. Those findings are usually real and are still not the work (V43), so a bounded loop caps them separately and treats a late-round scaffolding finding as a signal to end rather than a reason to spend another round.

finding_kind.description: `behavior` = it computes the wrong answer. `control-defeat` = it makes a gate unable to fail, or lets something bypass one (V4/V5 territory). `clerical` = naming, formatting, a stale comment. Only `control-defeat` accumulates toward the mechanism-class stop, because that is the class whose third instance means the mechanism is the defect (V30).

mechanism.description: Required for `control-defeat`: a stable kebab-case slug naming HOW the control was defeated, not the individual manoeuvre. Three blocking control-defeat findings sharing one mechanism refuse the next round — so the slug must be reused across rounds for the same underlying weakness. Examples: `unrun-validation-row`, `swallowed-exit-code`, `detector-without-fixture`, `empty-identity-propagated`.

command.description: The command that produced this result. Required for pass/fail/partial: a checklist row asserting an outcome with no command behind it is prose, and a gate that cannot be run cannot fail (V4). Omit only for `n/a`.

exit_code.description: The command's exit status. Recorded because exit 0 from a wrapper means the wrapper finished, not that the work happened (V2/V13) — keeping the number makes that distinction reviewable instead of assumed.

allOf.description: An approval may carry non-blocking findings, but not blocking ones. This is the v1 behaviour change: v1 required `findings: maxItems 0` to approve, which pushed reviewers into either suppressing real observations or withholding an approval the work had earned.
`changes_required` must name at least one blocking finding. A verdict that refuses without one is unactionable, and in practice it is how a reviewer records reluctance rather than a defect.
